classifications.item: OAuth/AuthService user identity, token rotation, replay grace, trusted-owner and session semantics
classifications.constraints: Remain the accepted control-plane user identity baseline. Device/agent identity is additive and may not weaken these semantics.
Move behind a platform-neutral SecretProtectorPort; keep DPAPI as the Windows implementation and add Keychain-backed macOS implementation.

classifications.item: PolicyEngine authorization, scopes, kill switch, emergency read-only and command policy
classifications.constraints: Preserve fail-closed V2 behavior while adding explicit device/agent target context and routing decisions.

classifications.item: AuditChain local HMAC chain and redaction
classifications.constraints: Preserve local tamper evidence and extend to distributed receipts containing workflow, node, attempt, resolved device and local receipt hash.
Add platform applicability, device locality, input/output contract identity and acceptance metadata; registry remains capability ownership authority, not scheduler.
Rehost as Windows agent capabilities behind DeviceAgentProtocol. Preserve policy bounds and process verification.
Become platform/device capability implementations; workflow core never imports OS-specific managers.

classifications.item: General SQLite store for auth, idempotency, sessions and local runtime state
classifications.constraints: Keep V2 security/session semantics. Canonical V3 workflow persistence is separately owned; V2 operator_jobs/operator_steps may not be authoritative V3 workflow state.
Replace on V3 code path with a thin Smart Operator Adapter that translates legacy plans to canonical DAG submissions/status. V2 branch remains untouched as rollback.
Preserve compatible public tools; list_devices becomes registry-backed and operator_* delegates to canonical workflow runtime.
Replace with first-class DeviceRegistry results; exact device identity must be explicit in acceptance.
Preserve manifest-bound verification and rollback semantics; extend orchestration to canary/staged fleet operations.
Retain local reliability behavior and add device/fleet health dimensions without centralizing workflow retry semantics.

classifications.item: Accepted V2 product release and rollback evidence
classifications.constraints: Immutable rollback/compatibility baseline until explicit V3 compatibility retirement.

classifications.reason: Taxonomy and executor boundary are useful; implementation only returns True and is not a real DAG executor.
Planner/order semantics are retained; implementation is a pass-through stub.
execute/resume boundary retained; implementation is a stub.
schedule/cancel boundary retained; implementation does not schedule.
State-machine ownership retained; transition implementation is a no-op.
Failure/recovery semantics are useful but incomplete for production workflow state.
Save/load ownership retained; implementation is not persistence.
Retry/recover boundary retained; production rules come from idempotency, state and exact outcome evidence.
Metrics/trace ownership retained; implementation is a stub.
Submit duration, success/failure, retry and recovery instrumentation are useful; replace in-memory/Python-specific mechanics with V3 observability ports.
Trigger boundary retained; implementation is a pass-through stub.
Explicit WorkflowStateStore abstraction is useful and provider-neutral.
Explicit scheduler port is useful but needs DAG readiness and resource-aware semantics.
Provider-neutral execution state, idempotency, timeout, scheduling and correlation semantics are valuable; adapt from tenant/provider model to Radlina subject/device/workflow model.
DurableWorkflowBridge/provider abstraction is useful. File contains duplicate test-provider definitions and is not suitable for copy-as-is.
Explicitly declares itself replaceability/test-only and not production evidence for durable orchestration; may inspire tests but cannot be canonical V3 engine.
Real durable provider bridge can become an optional external workflow-provider adapter; it is not the Smart Operator and does not own V3 product policy/device routing.
Not required for initial V3 core and some status/cancel boundaries are incomplete. Future provider-plugin candidates only.
Provider instrumentation decorator concept is useful behind V3 observability ports.
Execution duration, queue delay, retry and result metrics are retained semantically.

conclusion.canonical_decision: Reuse taxonomy/contracts and selected provider semantics; implement production-grade TypeScript workflow core under RRMW/CSEW with Smart Operator only as adapter.
forbidden: Copy stub workflow implementations as production code
Make Smart Operator a second scheduler/state store/retry engine
Treat NativeSQLiteWorkflowProvider as production durable-orchestration evidence
Make Temporal/Prefect/Airflow/Inngest the hidden owner of Radlina policy or device routing
